text:
elaine: quick sanity check — we saw a streaming client in Java throw a 401 after the svcacct JWT rotated. stream reconnects but then fails with 'audience mismatch'. has anyone hit this with our java-sdk + impersonation flow?

max: @elaine hmm, do you have the raw token a few lines from the app logs? sometimes the target_audience in the OIDC exchange is wrong so the STS returns a token with a different aud.

elaine: pasted a redacted snippet — logs below. the token audience is 'https://accounts.example.com' but our server expects 'https://api.redwood.ai/'.
```
2024-11-27T16:12:07Z INFO auth: fetching impersonated-token
2024-11-27T16:12:07Z DEBUG sts-request: target_audience="https://api.redwood.ai/"
2024-11-27T16:12:07Z DEBUG sts-response: access_token=*** aud="https://accounts.example.com"
2024-11-27T16:12:09Z WARN stream: stream reauth success; rpc error: UNAUTHENTICATED: token audience mismatch
```

samir: that log is the smoking gun. If the STS call is passing the wrong target_audience the returned token won't be valid for the downstream service. In Java flow we had two places: the ServiceAccountImpersonation helper and the streaming client. One can accidentally pass the internal 'sts' audience into the stream.

nate: short fix: ensure the OIDC exchange uses the full resource URL as audience. Example config (java):
```
ImpersonationOptions opts = ImpersonationOptions.newBuilder()
  .setTargetAudience("https://api.redwood.ai/")
  .setDelegates(List.of("projects/123/serviceAccounts/ops@..."))
  .build();
```
Also make sure the streaming token refresher uses the same opts instance.

elaine: noted. one wrinkle: when the stream rotates token mid-session the SDK does a silent refresh and tries to swap, but if the new token aud != expected the server closes and the client tries exponential-reconnect and then hits a 401 loop. should the SDK treat 401 during refresh as a non-retriable fatal for the session?

max: behavior depends. For short-lived passive requests we retry, but for long-lived streams it's safer to treat a 401 during token swap as a signal to tear down and re-init the stream (not just reauth in-place). We ended up implementing: on 401 from auth-swap -> close current stream and attempt a full stream reopen with a fresh token. avoids the mid-session half-baked state.

samir: Agreed. Also add a guard: if token's aud != service_aud then log and don't attempt in-place swap. Means you avoid the reconnect loop.

elaine: thanks — do we want a tiny unit/integration test in java-sdk for this? I can add one that fakes an STS returning wrong aud and asserts the stream restarts once and then errors.

nate: yes please. Test outline: 1) start fake server that expects aud X 2) start sdk streaming client with refresh callback that first returns valid token then returns token with aud Y 3) assert client closed and then attempts one full reopen and fails with UNAUTHN. Keep it flaky-resistant by counting attempts.

max: pinging @dev-bot to add a ticket so we don't lose this.

dev-bot: created RED-7821: java-sdk streaming: handle token-audience mismatch during refresh (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RED-7821) :white_check_mark:

elaine: perfect. i'll pick RED-7821 up after I finish the OIDC proxy fix. leaving notes in the PR when i push the test. :thumbsup:

max: thanks! if you want i can do a quick review on the test — @samir happy to pair on the guard logic.

samir: happy to pair tomorrow morning. :coffee:

elaine: awesome — will DM schedule. closing loop here.
